**Provenance**

- `CS-01` - Omnichannel Customer Care Agent: Web Chat, App, social inbox, Zalo, email and approved connectors (SRS section 8)
- `FR-CS-002` - Agent knows when to answer, when to look up, when to act, when to hand to another agent and when a human must take over (SRS section 8 (MUST))
- `FR-CS-001` - Recognise at least the ten required intents: product, price, stock, order status, shipping, return/exchange, payment, complaint, usage support, human request (SRS section 8 (MUST))

**Real-life risk.** Work begins without any recorded attempt, so a later escalation has no history and the customer repeats the same problem.

**Coverage facets**

- `entity:Service Case` - Service Case [entity, SRS section 14]
- `intent:order_status` - order_status [intent, SRS section 8] (requires FR-CS-001)
- `stage:ACTION` - ACTION [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)

**Preconditions**

1. An ASSIGNED order-status case CASE-T1-0003 for cust-a linked to ORD-A-1 in namespace cd-progress-*
2. Order lookup available through the stubbed ERP fixture

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "case_number": "CASE-T1-0003",
  "transition": {
    "event": "start_work",
    "actor": "CS-01"
  },
  "evidence": {
    "source": "ORD-A-1",
    "skill": "skill.care.lookup_order"
  }
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start work on the assigned case | state becomes IN_PROGRESS with a start timestamp and the owner unchanged |
| 2 | Record the lookup attempt against ORD-A-1 with its source reference | the case links an evidence record that references ORD-A-1 and the skill id used |
| 3 | Attempt to start work on a case that is still CLASSIFIED | the transition is refused as an invalid state transition and the case state is unchanged |
| 4 | Read the case timeline | the IN_PROGRESS transition and the evidence link appear once each in chronological order |

**Assertions**

- The case reports IN_PROGRESS with exactly one evidence link to ORD-A-1
- Starting work from CLASSIFIED is refused with an invalid-transition error
- The case timeline shows the transition and the evidence link exactly once each

**Forbidden**

- Report IN_PROGRESS without any recorded resolution attempt
- Overwrite the assigned owner while starting work

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Case projection and evidence link (source reference, skill id)
- Invalid-transition audit entry from the CLASSIFIED attempt

**Cleanup**

- Delete the run-scoped case and evidence link for cd-progress-*; keep the audit entries

**Automation seam.** Call the real manage_case skill with the ERP adapter stubbed by fixtures/offline/orders.json; assert on the evidence linkage rather than on the state string alone.

**Real-life risk.** A classified case is never owned by anyone, so no operator acts on it and the customer waits indefinitely.

  "case_number": "CASE-T1-0002",
  "assignment": {

  }
}

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Assign the classified case to owner CS-01 with an SLA due time | state becomes ASSIGNED, owner is CS-01 and sla_due_at equals the supplied value |
| 2 | Read the operator queue for tenant T1 | the case appears in queue support-shipping exactly once with its priority and SLA due time |
| 3 | Attempt a second assignment to a different owner without an unassign event | the reassignment is refused or produces an explicit reassignment audit entry, never a silent owner swap |
| 4 | Attempt to assign a case from tenant T2 to owner CS-01 of tenant T1 | the assignment is rejected and no cross-tenant ownership row is created |

- The case reports ASSIGNED with owner CS-01 and the exact SLA due time supplied
- The queue contains the case exactly once and the owner field is populated
- The cross-tenant assignment attempt leaves both tenants' case tables unchanged

**Forbidden**

- Leave the case unowned while reporting it as ASSIGNED
- Let an owner from another tenant appear on the case

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Case projection after assignment (owner, queue, sla_due_at)
- Queue listing entry plus the audit entries for the assignment attempts

**Cleanup**

- Unassign and delete the run-scoped case for cd-assign-*; keep audit history

### `INT-CASE-CONCURRENCY` - Two concurrent transitions on one case admit exactly one winner

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Suite | `integration/case-fsm.md` |
| Layer | integration |
| Environment | offline |
| Priority | critical |
| Gate | P1 |
| Basis | blueprint |
| Pair | - |
| Source module | `sources/platform.py` |
| Design status | `NOT_RUN` |

**Provenance**

- `CS-01` - Omnichannel Customer Care Agent: Web Chat, App, social inbox, Zalo, email and approved connectors (SRS section 8)
- `NFR-002` - Auditability: 100% of externally changing actions carry an audit/evidence record (SRS section 19 (MUST))
- `NFR-006` - Data isolation: customer A data never appears in customer B context (SRS section 19)

**Real-life risk.** Two operators act on the same case simultaneously, so the case ends in an impossible state and one operator's work silently disappears.

**Coverage facets**

- `entity:Service Case` - Service Case [entity, SRS section 14]
- `memory:Agent Operational Memory` - Agent Operational Memory [memory, SRS section 16]
- `stage:ACTION` - ACTION [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)

**Preconditions**

1. An IN_PROGRESS case CASE-T1-0010 for cust-a in namespace cd-race-*
2. Two concurrent transition requests issued at 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z by CS-01 (to RESOLVED) and op-7 (to WAITING_CUSTOMER)

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "case_number": "CASE-T1-0010",
  "requests": [
    {
      "actor": "CS-01",
      "to": "RESOLVED",
      "resolution_code": "refund_approved"
    },
    {
      "actor": "op-7",
      "to": "WAITING_CUSTOMER",
      "reason": "awaiting_photo"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Issue both transitions concurrently against the same case version | exactly one request succeeds and the other is rejected as a stale/concurrent transition |
| 2 | Read the resulting case state and its version | the case holds exactly one of the two target states and the version advanced by exactly one |
| 3 | Replay the losing request after the winner committed | the replay is refused against the new version and still does not change the state |
| 4 | Read the audit trail for the case | one accepted transition entry and at least one refused entry exist, each naming its actor |

**Assertions**

- Exactly one of the two concurrent transitions is accepted; the case version increases by exactly 1
- The losing request is refused without any partial write (no orphan resolution or reason field)
- The audit trail records both the accepted and the refused attempt with actor identity

**Forbidden**

- Apply both transitions so the case ends with a resolution and a waiting reason at once
- Let the losing request overwrite the winner's fields without a version check

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Case state, version and field-level projection after the race
- Audit entries for both attempts with accepted/refused status

**Cleanup**

- Delete the run-scoped case and its audit entries for the run window cd-race-*

**Automation seam.** Issue the two requests from two worker threads against the real case service behind the tenant-scoped wrapper; the version column and the field projection are the oracle, so a last-writer-wins implementation fails.

**Prerequisites**

- none beyond the offline toolchain

### `INT-CASE-EVIDENCE-LINK` - A case closure is traceable from trigger to evidence to outcome

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Suite | `integration/case-fsm.md` |
| Layer | integration |
| Environment | offline |
| Priority | high |
| Gate | P1 |
| Basis | blueprint |
| Pair | - |
| Source module | `sources/platform.py` |
| Design status | `NOT_RUN` |

**Provenance**

- `CS-01` - Omnichannel Customer Care Agent: Web Chat, App, social inbox, Zalo, email and approved connectors (SRS section 8)
- `BR-010` - Every important execution must produce evidence (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `TC-E2E-009` - Every successful action traces back Trigger, Context, Decision, Approval, Execution, Evidence, Outcome (SRS section 22)

**Real-life risk.** A closed case cannot be explained later, so the business cannot prove what the customer was told or whether the promise was kept.

**Coverage facets**

- `entity:Service Case` - Service Case [entity, SRS section 14]
- `entity:Evidence` - Evidence [entity, SRS section 14]
- `entity:Outcome` - Outcome [entity, SRS section 14]
- `stage:EVIDENCE` - EVIDENCE [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)

**Preconditions**

1. A case for cust-a resolved with refund_approved and linked to ORD-A-1 in namespace cd-trace-*
2. Traceability query executed for the case at 2026-01-16T12:00:00Z

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "case_number": "CASE-T1-0013",
  "expected_chain": [
    "trigger_event",
    "conversation_message",
    "decision",
    "action",
    "evidence",
    "outcome"
  ]
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Traverse the case traceability chain from the trigger to the outcome | each hop resolves to a concrete record id and the chain is unbroken end to end |
| 2 | Verify the evidence record backing the resolution | the evidence record carries a provider or system reference and its own identifier, and resolves to ORD-A-1 |
| 3 | Attempt to close a second case without linking any evidence record | the closure is refused because resolution requires evidence for a customer-impacting action |
| 4 | Compare the traceability chain before and after an attempted evidence edit | the edit is refused and the chain hashes are unchanged |

**Assertions**

- The chain resolves every hop from trigger to outcome with concrete record identifiers
- Closing a case with no evidence record is refused
- Evidence records are immutable: the edit attempt leaves the chain hash unchanged

**Forbidden**

- Close a customer-impacting case with no evidence record
- Rewrite or delete an evidence record after the case closed

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Traceability chain output for CASE-T1-0013 with record identifiers (redacted)
- Refusal entry for the evidence-less closure and the chain hash before/after the edit attempt

**Cleanup**

- Delete the run-scoped case and evidence rows for cd-trace-*; retain the linked audit chain for the run window

**Automation seam.** Query the real traceability projection over fixture records; the assertion walks the chain end to end instead of checking that a field exists.

### `INT-CASE-ILLEGAL` - CLOSED to CLASSIFIED is refused as an illegal transition

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Suite | `integration/case-fsm.md` |
| Layer | integration |
| Environment | offline |
| Priority | critical |
| Gate | P1 |
| Basis | baseline |
| Pair | - |
| Source module | `sources/platform.py` |
| Design status | `NOT_RUN` |

**Provenance**

- `CS-01` - Omnichannel Customer Care Agent: Web Chat, App, social inbox, Zalo, email and approved connectors (SRS section 8)
- `FR-CS-002` - Agent knows when to answer, when to look up, when to act, when to hand to another agent and when a human must take over (SRS section 8 (MUST))
- `NFR-002` - Auditability: 100% of externally changing actions carry an audit/evidence record (SRS section 19 (MUST))

**Real-life risk.** A closed case silently reopens into classification, so agents work a stale request and the reported reopen rate is understated.

**Coverage facets**

- `entity:Service Case` - Service Case [entity, SRS section 14]
- `stage:ACTION` - ACTION [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)

**Preconditions**

1. A CLOSED case CASE-T1-0007 for cust-a in namespace cd-illegal-*
2. Transition request sent by agent CS-01 with target state CLASSIFIED

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "case_number": "CASE-T1-0007",
  "illegal_transition": {
    "from": "CLOSED",
    "to": "CLASSIFIED",
    "actor": "CS-01"
  }
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Request CLOSED to CLASSIFIED without an explicit reopen decision | the transition is refused with an invalid-transition error and the case stays CLOSED |
| 2 | Request the same illegal transition with an unknown target state | the request is also refused and the case target state vocabulary is unchanged |
| 3 | Attempt the illegal transition from tenant T2 against the T1 case | the request returns no-row/not-found behavior and the T1 case is untouched |
| 4 | Read the case audit trail after the attempts | each refused attempt is recorded with its actor and the illegal previous/new state pair, and no state change entry exists |

**Assertions**

- The case reports CLOSED after every refusal and its transition history contains no CLOSED to CLASSIFIED entry
- Each refusal produces one audit entry naming the illegal transition pair
- A cross-tenant attempt returns no-row behavior without leaking the T1 case number

**Forbidden**

- Silently reopen a closed case through the ordinary classification path
- Suppress the refusal audit entry so the illegal attempt is invisible

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Case projection and transition count before/after the refusals
- Refusal audit entries with actor and the illegal state pair

**Cleanup**

- Delete the run-scoped case for cd-illegal-*; keep the refusal audit entries

**Automation seam.** Exercise the real state machine directly with illegal transitions; the oracle is the unchanged state plus the refusal audit trail, not the error message wording.

### `INT-CASE-IN_PROGRESS-to-WAITING_CUSTOMER` - Waiting for the customer pauses the case without losing the SLA

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Suite | `integration/case-fsm.md` |
| Layer | integration |
| Environment | offline |
| Priority | high |
| Gate | P1 |
| Basis | baseline |
| Pair | - |
| Source module | `sources/platform.py` |
| Design status | `NOT_RUN` |

**Provenance**

- `CS-01` - Omnichannel Customer Care Agent: Web Chat, App, social inbox, Zalo, email and approved connectors (SRS section 8)
- `FR-CS-002` - Agent knows when to answer, when to look up, when to act, when to hand to another agent and when a human must take over (SRS section 8 (MUST))
- `SRS-08` - Customer Care and Customer Success AI: omnichannel care, case management FSM and retention workflow (SRS section 8)

**Real-life risk.** The case waits forever with no customer-facing follow-up, or the SLA clock keeps running while the ball is in the customer's court.

**Coverage facets**

- `entity:Service Case` - Service Case [entity, SRS section 14]
- `intent:return_refund` - return_refund [intent, SRS section 8] (requires FR-CS-001)
- `kpi:Resolution Time` - Resolution Time [kpi, Customer Care, SRS section 20]

**Preconditions**

1. An IN_PROGRESS return case CASE-T1-0004 for cust-a in namespace cd-wait-*
2. Outbound follow-up question prepared for the customer

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "case_number": "CASE-T1-0004",
  "transition": {
    "event": "await_customer",
    "reason": "awaiting_return_photo"
  },
  "follow_up": {
    "message_ref": "msg_wait_1",
    "due_at": "2026-01-17T10:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Move the in-progress case to WAITING_CUSTOMER with a reason | state is WAITING_CUSTOMER and the reason is stored on the case |
| 2 | Ask the system for the automatic follow-up | exactly one follow-up is scheduled at the due time and the message reference is recorded on the case |
| 3 | Escalate the waiting case to a human operator | the case is escalated with its waiting state preserved and a new owner recorded, without a state regression |
| 4 | Compare the SLA fields before and after the wait transition | the SLA due time is unchanged or explicitly extended by policy, never silently cleared |

**Assertions**

- The case reports WAITING_CUSTOMER with reason awaiting_return_photo
- Exactly one follow-up is scheduled and referenced on the case
- sla_due_at is unchanged after the transition or carries an explicit policy extension reason

**Forbidden**

- Leave WAITING_CUSTOMER without any scheduled follow-up
- Clear the SLA due time to hide a breach

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Case projection with state, reason, owner and SLA fields
- Scheduled follow-up record plus any extension audit entry

**Cleanup**

- Cancel the run-scoped follow-up and delete the case for cd-wait-*; retire the message reference only if it was never dispatched

**Automation seam.** Run the real manage_case skill with a deterministic scheduler; the oracle combines the case projection with the scheduled follow-up so a case parked without follow-up fails.

**Real-life risk.** An inbound request is never classified, so it stays invisible to the queue and breaches first-response commitments silently.

**Coverage facets**

- `entity:Service Case` - Service Case [entity, SRS section 14]
- `intent:shipping` - shipping [intent, SRS section 8] (requires FR-CS-001)
- `stage:SIGNAL` - SIGNAL [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)

**Preconditions**

1. Tenant T1 with a conversation for cust-a carrying the utterance 'my order has not arrived' in namespace cd-case-*
2. Case created at 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with priority P3 default

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "customer_id": "cust-a",
  "case": {
    "case_number": "CASE-T1-0001",
    "state": "NEW",
    "priority": "P3"
  },
  "transition": {
    "event": "classify",
    "intent": "shipping",
    "priority": "P2"
  }
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Create the case from the inbound utterance and read its initial projection | state is NEW, priority P3, and the case is linked to the conversation and to cust-a |
| 2 | Apply the classification transition with intent shipping and priority P2 | the case reports state CLASSIFIED, intent shipping, priority P2 and a state-change timestamp after creation |
| 3 | Read the audit trail for the case | exactly one NEW to CLASSIFIED entry exists with the actor, the previous state and the new state |
| 4 | Re-apply the identical classification event | the case stays CLASSIFIED and the audit gains no second transition for that event identity |

**Assertions**

- The case projection reports CLASSIFIED with intent shipping and priority P2
- Exactly one audit entry records the NEW to CLASSIFIED transition
- The duplicate classification produces zero additional transitions and does not regress the state

**Forbidden**

- Accept a classification with an intent outside the ten supported intents
- Skip NEW and write a case directly in CLASSIFIED with no audit entry

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Case projection before and after classification (state, intent, priority, timestamps)
- Audit entries for the case with actor and previous/new state

**Cleanup**

- Delete the run-scoped case and its conversation link for cd-case-*; keep the append-only audit entries

**Automation seam.** Drive the real case-management skill against fixture conversations, freezing the clock so ordering is deterministic; state the oracle on the projection and the audit count, not on the enum definition.

### `INT-CASE-REOPEN` - A closed case reopens through the explicit reopen branch

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Suite | `integration/case-fsm.md` |
| Layer | integration |
| Environment | offline |
| Priority | medium |
| Gate | P1 |

**Provenance**

- `CS-01` - Omnichannel Customer Care Agent: Web Chat, App, social inbox, Zalo, email and approved connectors (SRS section 8)
- `FR-CS-002` - Agent knows when to answer, when to look up, when to act, when to hand to another agent and when a human must take over (SRS section 8 (MUST))
- `FR-CS-003` - Retention workflow: Signal, Hypothesis, Recommended Action, Eligibility Check, Execution/Approval, Outcome (SRS section 8 (MUST))

**Real-life risk.** A dissatisfied customer cannot reopen a closed case, so the complaint is lost and the reopen KPI is wrong. The blueprint names a REOPENED branch while the SRS lists only the seven minimum states, so the transition here is proposed configuration.

**Coverage facets**

- `entity:Service Case` - Service Case [entity, SRS section 14]
- `kpi:Reopen Rate` - Reopen Rate [kpi, Customer Care, SRS section 20]
- `intent:complaint` - complaint [intent, SRS section 8] (requires FR-CS-001)

**Preconditions**

1. A CLOSED case CASE-T1-0008 for cust-a in namespace cd-reopen-*
2. Tenant policy publish_case_reopen enabled with a 30 day reopen window

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "case_number": "CASE-T1-0008",
  "reopen_event": {
    "reason": "customer_complaint",
    "within_days": 12,
    "actor": "CS-01"
  },
  "closed_at": "2026-01-04T10:00:00Z"
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Apply the explicit reopen event inside the policy window | the case enters REOPENED with the previous resolution retained and a reopen timestamp recorded |
| 2 | Apply an identical reopen event again | no second reopen entry is produced and the case stays REOPENED |
| 3 | Attempt a reopen 45 days after closure | the reopen is refused by the window policy and the case stays CLOSED |
| 4 | Read the reopen KPI input for the tenant | the reopened case is counted exactly once in the Reopen Rate numerator for the period |

**Assertions**

- The in-window reopen produces state REOPENED with one reopen audit entry and the original resolution preserved
- The out-of-window reopen is refused and the case stays CLOSED
- The Reopen Rate input counts the case exactly once

**Forbidden**

- Reopen a closed case while discarding the previous resolution or its evidence
- Count the same reopen twice in the KPI input

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Case projection after each reopen attempt with the retained resolution reference
- Reopen Rate input rows for the tenant period

**Cleanup**

- Delete the run-scoped reopen rows for cd-reopen-*; restore the policy flag to its fixture value

**Automation seam.** Run the real state machine with the reopen branch enabled by tenant policy; because the SRS fixes only the minimum states, this case is labelled a proposed configuration and must not be reported as SRS-mandated.

<a id="case-int-case-resolved-to-closed"></a>

### `INT-CASE-RESOLVED-to-CLOSED` - A resolved case closes after the confirmation window and stays immutable

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Suite | `integration/case-fsm.md` |
| Layer | integration |
| Environment | offline |
| Priority | high |
| Gate | P1 |
| Basis | baseline |
| Pair | - |
| Source module | `sources/platform.py` |
| Design status | `NOT_RUN` |

**Provenance**

- `CS-01` - Omnichannel Customer Care Agent: Web Chat, App, social inbox, Zalo, email and approved connectors (SRS section 8)
- `NFR-002` - Auditability: 100% of externally changing actions carry an audit/evidence record (SRS section 19 (MUST))
- `SRS-08` - Customer Care and Customer Success AI: omnichannel care, case management FSM and retention workflow (SRS section 8)

**Real-life risk.** Cases stay open forever, or a closed case is edited so the audit trail no longer reflects what the customer was told.

**Coverage facets**

- `entity:Service Case` - Service Case [entity, SRS section 14]
- `kpi:Reopen Rate` - Reopen Rate [kpi, Customer Care, SRS section 20]
- `stage:OUTCOME` - OUTCOME [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)

**Preconditions**

1. A RESOLVED case CASE-T1-0006 for cust-a resolved at 2026-01-16T09:10:00Z in namespace cd-close-*
2. 54 hours pass with no customer reply before the close transition

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "case_number": "CASE-T1-0006",
  "closed_at": "2026-01-18T15:10:00Z",
  "confirmation_window_hours": 48
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Close the resolved case after the confirmation window | state becomes CLOSED with a closed_at timestamp after the resolution timestamp |
| 2 | Attempt to edit the resolution text and the owner of the closed case | the edits are refused and the closed case content is unchanged |
| 3 | Attempt a reply to the closed case | the reply does not reopen the case implicitly and is routed for explicit reopen handling |
| 4 | Read the case audit trail after the close | the full transition history is intact, including resolution and close entries with their actors |

**Assertions**

- The case reports CLOSED with closed_at later than the resolution timestamp
- Post-close edits are refused and the case content hash is unchanged
- The audit trail still contains every earlier transition entry

**Forbidden**

- Modify a closed case's resolution or owner
- Delete any case transition entry to make the history look cleaner

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Closed case projection with closed_at and content hash before/after the edit attempts
- Refusal audit entries for the post-close edit and reply attempts

**Cleanup**

- Delete the run-scoped closed case for cd-close-*; retain its immutable audit history for the run window

**Automation seam.** Freeze the clock to cross the confirmation window deterministically and run the real case skill; the oracle includes the content hash so silent edits cannot pass.

### `INT-CASE-SKIP-DENIED` - Skipping required states is refused while the documented reopen path still works

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Suite | `integration/case-fsm.md` |
| Layer | integration |
| Environment | offline |
| Priority | high |
| Gate | P1 |
| Basis | blueprint |
| Pair | - |
| Source module | `sources/platform.py` |
| Design status | `NOT_RUN` |

**Provenance**

- `CS-01` - Omnichannel Customer Care Agent: Web Chat, App, social inbox, Zalo, email and approved connectors (SRS section 8)
- `FR-CS-002` - Agent knows when to answer, when to look up, when to act, when to hand to another agent and when a human must take over (SRS section 8 (MUST))
- `SRS-08` - Customer Care and Customer Success AI: omnichannel care, case management FSM and retention workflow (SRS section 8)

**Real-life risk.** A case is forced straight to RESOLVED to hit a metric, hiding the fact that no agent ever worked it.

**Coverage facets**

- `entity:Service Case` - Service Case [entity, SRS section 14]
- `stage:APPROVAL` - APPROVAL [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)

**Preconditions**

1. A NEW case CASE-T1-0009 for cust-a in namespace cd-skip-*
2. Tenant policy allows only the documented forward transitions plus the REOPENED branch

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "case_number": "CASE-T1-0009",
  "attempts": [
    {
      "from": "NEW",
      "to": "RESOLVED"
    },
    {
      "from": "NEW",
      "to": "CLOSED"
    },
    {
      "from": "IN_PROGRESS",
      "to": "NEW"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Attempt NEW to RESOLVED and NEW to CLOSED directly | both are refused with an invalid-transition error and the case remains NEW |
| 2 | Walk the documented forward path one state at a time | each documented transition is accepted in order: CLASSIFIED, ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_CUSTOMER, RESOLVED, CLOSED |
| 3 | Attempt one backward transition (IN_PROGRESS to NEW) on a second case | the backward transition is refused and that case keeps its state |
| 4 | Read both cases' transition histories | the refused skips appear only as refusal audit entries and the accepted path appears as one entry per step |

**Assertions**

- All three skip/backward attempts are refused with no state change
- The stepwise path completes all seven states with one audit entry per accepted transition
- No case reaches RESOLVED without having passed IN_PROGRESS

**Forbidden**

- Allow an unconfigured skip so a metric looks better
- Permit a backward transition that silently rewrites the earlier history

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Transition history for the case in each attempt with accepted/refused status
- Case projection after the full forward path

**Cleanup**

- Delete the run-scoped cases for cd-skip-*; keep refusal and transition audit entries

**Automation seam.** Run the real state machine once with the documented configuration; the case treats the SRS minimum states as the requirement and reports any additional allowed transition as proposed configuration.

### `INT-CASE-SLA-BREACH` - SLA breach and priority ordering are observable on the case queue

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Suite | `integration/case-fsm.md` |
| Layer | integration |
| Environment | offline |
| Priority | high |
| Gate | P1 |
| Basis | blueprint |
| Pair | - |
| Source module | `sources/platform.py` |
| Design status | `NOT_RUN` |

**Provenance**

- `CS-01` - Omnichannel Customer Care Agent: Web Chat, App, social inbox, Zalo, email and approved connectors (SRS section 8)
- `NFR-009` - Performance: normal conversation is designed for near real-time response; the official SLA is locked after benchmarking (SRS section 19)
- `SRS-20` - KPI system: the thirty-two metrics across five groups (SRS section 20)

**Real-life risk.** Breached cases are invisible in the queue, so customers with the oldest problems keep waiting while the dashboard reports a healthy service level.

**Coverage facets**

- `entity:Service Case` - Service Case [entity, SRS section 14]
- `kpi:Resolution Time` - Resolution Time [kpi, Customer Care, SRS section 20]
- `kpi:First Response Time` - First Response Time [kpi, Customer Care, SRS section 20]

**Preconditions**

1. Tenant T1 with four cases at priorities P1..P4 and sla_due_at 2026-01-15T18:00:00Z in namespace cd-sla-*
2. Queue read at 2026-01-15T19:30:00Z, after two due times have passed

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "cases": [
    {
      "case_number": "CASE-T1-0011",
      "priority": "P1",
      "sla_due_at": "2026-01-15T11:00:00Z"
    },
    {
      "case_number": "CASE-T1-0012",
      "priority": "P4",
      "sla_due_at": "2026-01-15T18:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "read_at": "2026-01-15T19:30:00Z"
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Read the case queue ordered by priority and SLA due time | P1 cases precede P4 cases, and within a priority the earliest sla_due_at comes first |
| 2 | Read the breach flags at the observation timestamp | CASE-T1-0011 is flagged breached with the elapsed overrun and CASE-T1-0012 is not flagged |
| 3 | Attempt to assign priority P5 to a case | the assignment is refused and the priority vocabulary stays P1..P4 |
| 4 | Read the Resolution Time and First Response Time inputs for the breached case | both inputs are derived from the case timestamps and the breach is reflected rather than hidden |

**Assertions**

- The queue ordering matches priority then earliest due time, with the breached P1 case first
- Exactly one of the two cases is flagged breached at the observation timestamp
- Resolution Time and First Response Time inputs reflect the case timestamps including the breach

**Forbidden**

- Hide a breached case from the operator queue
- Accept a priority outside P1..P4

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- Queue listing with priority, sla_due_at and breach flag per case
- KPI input rows for the breached case (first response and resolution timings)

**Cleanup**

- Delete the run-scoped cases for cd-sla-*; keep KPI inputs for the run window only

**Automation seam.** Freeze the clock at a point after the due time so breach detection is deterministic; the oracle is the queue ordering and the breach flag, both read through the real projection.
